records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:19 defines feed_key (feed-modified: cache key) but never uses it, so the feed is refetched and all items reimported hourly with no conditional GET
records.rationale: The feed_key method is indeed defined and never called, but the claimed harm — 'all items reimported hourly' — is contradicted by the diff itself: TopicEmbed.import looks up an existing embed by embed_url ('embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first') and only revises the post when 'content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1'. So unchanged items are not reimported; the only residual issue is a dead helper method plus skipping a conditional GET, which is a style/efficiency nit, not the described defect.

records.rationale: The diff adds `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in post.rb, imports external RSS/article HTML via TopicEmbed.import with no sanitization step, and renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in embed/best.html.erb. Content from an external feed/URL is thus stored and served as raw HTML, a plausible stored XSS path fully grounded in the diff.

records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 edits an already-shipped migration to use `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which drops the existing table and its data if re-run
records.rationale: The diff indeed shows `create_table :top_topics` changed to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in an existing (dated) migration. `force: true` drops the table if it exists, so re-running the migration would silently drop top_topics data; editing already-shipped migrations is a real data-loss/correctness hazard. This is grounded directly in the diff lines.

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:44 calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously inside a per-URL retrieval job, blocking one embed request on fetching and importing an entire feed
records.rationale: Verified in the diff: lib/topic_retriever.rb perform_retrieve calls 'Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})' synchronously rather than enqueueing it, and PollFeed polls the entire RSS feed and imports every item. So one embed retrieval request can block on fetching and importing a whole feed — an accurate, specific performance/architecture concern grounded in the added code, though not strictly a correctness defect.

records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:41-46 asserts TopicRetriever.new/retrieve are called, but the controller enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic, so the test exercises nothing real
records.rationale: The diff shows the controller enqueues the job (`Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` in embed_controller.rb) rather than constructing a TopicRetriever inline, while the spec (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb) mocks `TopicRetriever.new`/`retrieve` being invoked synchronously. In the test environment there is no indication Jobs.enqueue executes inline, so these expectations do not match the production code path and the test does not verify real behavior. The mechanism is visible in the diff; the only uncertainty is whether the test harness runs jobs inline
